statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: two distinct weakenings. (i) NO COMPARISON CELL — the book requires the SPECIFIC pair (L ∘ Lan_K F, Lη) to satisfy the universal property, i.e. that the canonical comparison 2-cell induced by whiskering the unit be the extension; the in-tree definition only asserts that the two functors are naturally isomorphic (≈ on functors is `Functor_Setoid`, i.e. an unconstrained natural isomorphism, Theory/Functor.v:148) with no mention of η or of any coherence between the iso and the units. A functor could satisfy the in-tree condition by accident while failing the book's. (ii) GLOBAL-ONLY — the hypotheses are the class `LeftKan K` (`Lan ⊣ Induced`, Theory/Kan/Extension.v:222), i.e. the extension must exist for EVERY diagram simultaneously as an adjoint, on both sides; the book's notion applies to a single (possibly merely local) Kan extension. The in-tree definition cannot even be stated for `LocalLeftKan X` / `LocalRightKan X` (lines 234, 154), which is exactly the generality Definitions 6.3.5/6.3.6 need to define pointwise Kan extensions by preservation under representables.

gap: The in-tree `preserves_left_Kan`/`preserves_right_Kan` (a) drop the unit/comparison-cell clause, asserting a bare natural isomorphism of the two extending functors rather than that (L ∘ Lan_K F, Lη) enjoys the universal property, and (b) are quantified over GLOBAL Kan extensions (the adjoint classes `LeftKan`/`RightKan`) on both sides, so preservation of a single LOCAL Kan extension — the form Def 6.3.5/6.3.6 require — is not expressible.
